blocks.prompt: 5 (i) From a deck of 13 cards, find in how many ways these are arranging in a rectangular form? Hint (order is matter) All cards.
blocks.explanation:
All 13 different cards are placed in 13 positions; the hint says order matters.
We must count the arrangements.
Plan: arranging all \(n\) things gives \({}^{n}P_{n} = n!\), so the answer is \(13!\).
steps:
Given: 13 different cards, all of them placed.
To find: number of arrangements.
Method: \({}^{13}P_{13} = \frac{13!}{0!} = 13!\).

Build \(13!\) from \(10!\)
\[10! = 3628800\]
\[11! = 11 \times 3628800 = 39916800\]
\[12! = 12 \times 39916800 = 479001600\]
Why: \(n! = n \times (n-1)!\), so each factorial comes from the one before it.

Finish
\[13! = 13 \times 479001600\]
\[= 6227020800\]
Why: Multiply once more by 13.

Check
\[13 \times 479001600 = 4790016000 + 1437004800\]
\[= 6227020800 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Split 13 as \(10 + 3\) and add the two products.

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) From a deck of 13 cards, find in how many ways these are arranging in a rectangular form? Hint (order is matter) 8 cards.
blocks.explanation:
Now only 8 of the 13 cards are placed, in order.
We must count the arrangements.
Plan: \({}^{13}P_{8}\) = product of 8 numbers from 13 down to 6.
steps:
Check
\[13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11 \cdot 10 = 17160\]
\[9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 = 3024\]
\[17160 \times 3024 = 51891840 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The 8 factors 13 down to 6, multiplied in two groups, give the same result.

blocks.prompt: 5 (iii) From a deck of 13 cards, find in how many ways these are arranging in a rectangular form? Hint (order is matter) 10 cards.
blocks.explanation:
10 of the 13 cards are placed in order.
We must count the arrangements.
Plan: \({}^{13}P_{10} = \frac{13!}{3!}\).
